Resolution requires separating concerns: cluster balancing (safety-critical), algebraic optimization with multivaluedness constraints (requires formal correctness proof), and error messaging (usability improvement).

Conversely, strict cluster balancing requirements may limit the performance gains from vectorization. This represents a classic trade-off between performance optimization (trustworthiness through speed/efficiency) and operational stability (responsibility through consistency/transparency).

These are orthogonal concerns requiring separate resolution paths. The safety requirements do not directly validate or contradict the responsibility requirements; rather, they operate in different technical domains.
